  STAFF REPORT ITEM No. 1
To:  Honorable Parks & Recreation Commission
From:  Tina Fierro, Deputy Director
Date:  April 24, 2025

Subject:  Aquatics Summer Programs Review

Recommended Motion:  Motion to receive and file.

Report Summary:

The Aquatics Division is proud to report another successful and impactful year spanning
from Summer 2024 through Spring 2025. This period was marked by increased
community participation, program innovation, improved safety protocols, and strong
staff development. Our continued commitment to accessible, high-quality aquatic
services has resulted in both measurable outcomes and positive community feedback.

The year began with an extremely busy Summer 2024 season, highlighted by an almost
20% increase in swim program enrollment compared to the previous summer. More
than 2,800 individuals participated, reflecting a growing demand for water safety, swim
instruction, and specialized aquatic programs. Our most popular program, Learn-to-
Swim (consisting of Group, Private, and Semi-Private swim lessons for all ages) was at
full capacity every month. Our Summer Splash Camp for Kids is growing in popularity;
we saw a 20% increase in participation and had close to 100 participants. We also
gained traction with our aquatic sports programs like Junior Water Polo, Junior
Lifeguard, Surfing 101, and Gators Swim Academy. We continued to host competitive
swim teams South Gate Aqua Coalition (SGAC), Penguins Aquatic Club (PAC), and
Lynwood Marlins (LMST), providing over 250 hours of practice time for approximately
200 kids. With expanded hours, we were able to bring back seasonal aquatic fitness
programs in addition to offering our year-round fitness and therapy classes; our line-up
featured SeniorCise, Aqua Aerobics, Masters Swim, Open Play Water Polo and Aqua
Blast. To promote these programs, we presented our first ever Aquatic Fitness Expo
and launched the Splash Fitness membership.

Summer is an extremely popular season for party rentals as well, and we were able to
accommodate over 20 private parties. We also offered free water safety awareness
events throughout the summer, including the World’s Largest Swimming Lesson in June
  Page 1 of 4

  4
 and three Community Swim Days: Summer Kick-Off Splash event in June, 4th of July
Splash event in July, and Back-to-School Splash event in August. These special events
cumulatively brought in around 500 community members. Overall attendance remained
high, with over 30,000 visits recorded during the summer months for Lap Swim, Adult
Swim and Family Swim sessions.

During the fall months, our indoor aquatic programming continued to thrive. While we
offer fewer programs in the off-season, our Learn-to-Swim program maintained
consistent demand and remained at capacity, seeing only a minor dip come November.
We served over 1,500 patrons during this period between our Group, Private, and Semi-
Private swim lessons. We brought back the Pre-Competitive Swim Class, which is our
most advanced swim lesson program for youth and our best feeder program into the
competitive swim teams. We continued to provide almost 250 hours of pool time to
partner organization South Gate Aqua Coalition (SGAC), Penguins Aquatic Club (PAC)
and Lynwood Marlins Swim Team (LMST). Additionally, as the home pool to the South
Central Swim League’s fall league, we hosted six meets during this season, with each
meet bringing in about six local swim teams, 400 local competitive swimmers, and over
600 spectators. We also served as host to SGAC’s invitational USA swimming meet in
September, which brought in approximately 500 swimmers and their families and
served as a fundraiser for the team.

All aquatic staff maintained up-to-date certifications in Lifeguard Training, CPR, and
First Aid. Monthly in-service training emphasized emergency readiness, inclusive
customer service, and continuous improvement. We offered one Adult and Pediatric
First Aid/CPR/AED course, which teaches students how to respond to breathing and
cardiac emergencies. We certified almost 15 community and staff members this round.
SeniorCise, Aqua Aerobics, Masters Swim, and Aqua Blast fitness classes remained in
rotation, with Open Play Water Polo wrapping up in October. We had our second annual
Patti’s Pumpkin Plunge, our floating pumpkin patch, featuring arts and crafts, a pumpkin
decorating contest, games, prizes, music and more. We completely sold out at 200
participants.

The Aquatics Division sustained solid performance across all areas of operation during
the winter season, despite the seasonal challenges that typically affect participation and
facility maintenance. Our Learn-to-Swim program takes a break in the winter, but the
remaining programs saw steady attendance, our staff remained committed to safety and
professional development, and our facilities continued to serve the community
effectively. Water fitness and therapeutic classes continued to be a vital service,
particularly for older adults. With almost 80 sessions offered throughout the quarter,
programs such as Aqua Blast, Aqua Aerobics, and SeniorCise were well attended. The
Pre-Competitive Swim Class remained strong, with kids working hard to make the
transition to the swim team. As one of the only indoor pools open year-round, we were
able to continue hosting local swim teams’ practices, the South-Central Swim League’s
winter swim league, and 3 USA Swimming meets including the prestigious WAG Last
Ditch Qualifier 2-day meet. This meet brought in approximately 800 swimmers and over
1,500 spectators per day from more than a dozen teams coming from the wider Los
Angeles area; we were able to bring this bigger meet to South Gate due to recent
fencing and other capital expenditure projects that made it possible to expand our patio
  Page 2 of 4

  5
 space. The Aquatics Team held the second annual special holiday event, Surfing with
Santa. This special day featured arts and crafts, games, activities, prizes, and an
opportunity to surf with Santa, Mrs. Claus, and their elves. We sold-out this event too, at
200 participants.

Staff development and safety remained top priorities. During this quarter, one lifeguard
certification course was conducted, resulting in 4 newly certified lifeguards. Monthly in-
service trainings ensured that all lifeguards remained sharp and prepared. Cashier and
swim instructor trainings helped improve the quality of our programs, operations, and
customer service. All aquatic staff completed Mandated Reporter training. We brought
back our Senior Lifeguard Training/Mentorship Program, with the goal of facilitating
staff’s professional development, skill enhancement, and career advancement. We had
8 mentees/mentors participate in the 6-week program, which culminated with interviews
for the Senior Lifeguard position. We are happy to report that we are promoting 6 of the
participants. During this quarter, our facility recorded zero major incidents, and all safety
equipment, including CPR and AED units, were regularly inspected and maintained in
full working order. Facility maintenance was another focus, and while routine
maintenance is performed year-round, the Aquatics Staff took the slower season as an
opportunity to deep clean the patron locker-rooms, staff areas, deck, and patio.

Things start to get busier again in the spring, especially with the return of our most
popular program, Learn-to-Swim Group, Private, and Semi-Private swim lessons for all
ages. March started off strong, with over 500 registrations. We also launched a new
program, Youth & Adult Swim Clinic with the focus of teaching participants water
competency and survival skills versus the traditional swim lesson curriculum. We had
over 20 participants and garnered a lot of interest for another round of this program. We
offered a variety of safety training courses for the community. During this period, we
held three different Adult and Pediatric First Aid/CPR/AED courses and two different
Lifeguard Certification courses. As first responders, Aquatics Staff is consistently
training, and in May-June we will once again have our annual recertification course
certifying 50 Lifeguards in American Red Cross Lifeguarding with CPR/AED For
Professional Rescuers, First Aid, Administering Emergency Oxygen, and Bloodborne
Pathogens Training.

This season, we again serve as host to SCSL’s spring swim league with 6 meets in our
schedule. High School Swim is also back, with South East High School practicing at our
pool. They have approximately 40 swimmers and 4 meets in their program. April was
especially eggciting, as we introduced another special aquatics event, Easter Splash
Fest. This event was met with much success, selling out at almost 250 participants. We
partnered with Raising Canes and SGAC, and had an underwater egg hunt as well as
one in our grass area. We had goodie bags, arts and crafts, lawn games, and a giant
Easter bunny bounce house. Also in April, we partnered with a local school for their
College & Career Day. Aquatics Staff presented kids with goodie bags, info on how to
obtain a career within aquatics, and gave water safety & first aid demos. It was a great
success and one we will continue to build on. May is designated as National Water
Safety Month, so the Swim Stadium in partnership with the Parks & Rec Social Media
Team is campaigning all month long to bring water safety awareness to the community.
We were honored to receive Council’s proclamation recognizing May as Water Safety
  Page 3 of 4

  6
 Month. We’re celebrating International Water Safety Day on May 15 and are hosting our
6th Annual Water Safety Bash on May 17; it’s a free event for the whole community.

In conclusion, the Aquatics Division made meaningful progress during the 2024–2025
year across all areas of service. Plans for the 2025–2026 cycle include expanding
adaptive aquatics & aquatic fitness classes, increasing lifeguard recruitment outreach,
and integrating more community partnerships.

  STAFF REPORT ITEM No. 2
To:  Honorable Parks & Recreation Commission
From:  Glenn Massey, Parks Superintendent
Date:  April 24, 2025

Subject:  Third Quarter Review of Grounds & Facility Maintenance FY 2024/25

Recommended Motion:  Motion to receive and file.

Report Summary:

Grounds Maintenance
During this quarter 60 azaleas were planted in the Azalea Garden, adjacent to the
Senior Citizen Building, and the tree trimming at Hollydale Regional Park was
completed.

The baseball diamonds and soccer field renovations were completed this quarter. Three
French drains were installed behind ball diamond number 9 to improve drainage and dry
the soil in the surrounding area. We reseeded the adjacent turf, added decomposed
granite, and a boulder to beautify the area.

Staff completed the renovation of the decomposed granite pathways and the turf
improvements on the westside area parks, State Street Park and Cesar Chavez Park.
The turf renovations consist of mowing the turf low, inspecting and repairing irrigation
systems, and reseeding.

Staff has also assisted the Police Department with the cleanup and removal of several
homeless encampments on the westside area parks this quarter.

We hosted the Azalea Car Show, held at the Golf Course, grounds staff set up the show
mobile and assisted the management team with the event.

We continue to host monthly food giveaways for the community at Hollydale Regional
Park, which are well attended.

Staff continues servicing and beautifying over 190 acres of park land daily.

  Page 1 of 2

  8
 Park Facility Maintenance
Parks Facility Maintenance staff set up and hosted a variety of Azalea Festival events,
Earth Day at South Gate Park and Hollydale Regional Park, Easter Egg Hunt in the Golf
Course, Women’s Club Annual Conference, the grand opening of Hollydale Community
Park just to mention a few.

Due to the high use of SG Park, Staff continues to do a third daily inspection and
cleaning, in the late afternoon to our outdoor restrooms. We have continued the use of
Electrostatic Disinfecting Equipment for more coverage in our cleaning and disinfecting
efforts for both indoor and outdoor restroom facilities, along with a pressure washing
program. These disinfecting and cleaning tools will be used consistently.

Set-ups for all events require us to disinfect all tables, chairs, door handles, and A/V
equipment.

We welcomed a new Park Facility Maintenance Worker to the team. This new position
has been crucial in covering weekend shifts, enhancing our ability to maintain park
facilities consistently throughout the week.

Additionally, we had privacy walls installed in our outdoor restrooms at State Street and
Cesar Chavez Parks. This improvement allows us to leave restroom doors in the open
position, addressing safety concerns and preventing users from inadvertently locking
themselves in restrooms for extended periods.

To accommodate the growing number of classes, reservations, and events, staff
schedules have been adjusted to ensure full coverage and support. Facility staff has
displayed exceptional flexibility and professionalism in managing the transition between
regular operations and new demands, consistently responding to the evolving needs of
the Division.

The Community Service Worker program is ongoing; we are still limiting the intake to 15
people maximum per day.

Parks are busy with many events, classes, picnics, and sports activities. We remain
vigilant when addressing the ongoing challenges with restroom cleanliness with a
routine restroom disinfecting program. This includes the use of the C3 Machine to apply
disinfectants and cleaners. Once the product is sprayed, staff scrubs floors, walls, and
fixtures to insure sanitary conditions

  STAFF REPORT ITEM No. 3
To:  Honorable Parks & Recreation Commission
From:  Steve Costley, Director of Parks & Rec.
Date:  April 23, 2025
Subject:  Recreation Programing Report – 3rd Quarter Review FY 2024/25

Recommended Motion: Motion to Receive and File

Report Summary:

Aquatics
The Aquatics Division had a productive third quarter, focused on facility maintenance,
winter operations, programming, and staff development. Attendance remained steady
despite seasonal slowdowns, and preparation for spring programming began
immediately after the holidays.

The Aquatics Team deep cleaned the locker rooms, office areas, storage room, and
general pool deck. Public Works completed routine maintenance on the pool and spa,
along with minor repairs to plumbing in the locker rooms. Lastly, new signage for safety
protocols and rules were installed.

The Swim Stadium is open 7 days a week year-round, with several Adult, Lap, and
Family Swim sessions available throughout the day. We had over 5,000 visits during
our recreational swim hours for this period; 4,000 from member scan-ins and almost
1,000 from daily admissions. We also had over 3,000 active memberships, with the
majority being Adult and Senior Splash Memberships.

We continued to host 3 local swim teams through the winter: partner organization South
Gate Aqua Coalition (SGAC), Lynwood Marlins Swim Team (LMST), and Penguins
Aquatic Club (PAC). SGAC practices 5x week, LMST 4x week, and PAC 3x week.
Cumulatively, teams bring in approximately 120 youth swimmers per day. In February,
SGAC hosted a USA Swimming meet with 5 local teams and almost 500 participants
plus their families. We also hosted the South-Central Swim League's 2-day winter
championships back in January and are hosting their spring league. Each meet brings
in over 6 local teams with almost 1,000 participants and spectators.

  Page 1 of 7
  10
 In January and February, we had the Pre-Competitive Swim Class, which is the most
advanced swim lesson level we offer and serves as the best feeder program for the club
swim teams. In March, we hosted a Youth & Adult Swim Lesson Clinic with the focus of
better preparing participants for the Learn-to-Swim program season ahead. This
program aims at making everyone water competent- meaning, it helps people overcome
their fear of water and teaches some basic water survival skills. We had almost 30
participants in the program. Also in March, we kicked off our Learn-to-Swim program
which includes group, private and semi-private swim lessons for all ages. This program
runs March through November and consistently maximizes registrations every session.
While we serve all age groups, most registrations continue to be for youth ages 6-17.
Aquatic Fitness classes continued through the winter, and although we did see a dip in
our attendance numbers, we are getting creative with the classes offered for the spring
season to attract a bigger variety of participants.

The slower winter season allows us to focus on a lot of staff development. We held 3
in-service trainings during this period, with a focus on CPR/AED, deep-water rescues,
spinal rescues, and other related emergency drills. We conducted a swim instructor
training to go over changes to the swim lesson curriculum. Lastly, full-time aquatics
staff were heavily involved in the greater aquatics’ community during this quarter: the
Aquatics Supervisor served on the Southern California Public Pool Operator
Association’s Board of Directors as a Member-at-Large and assisted with the planning
of the 2025 Surf and Turf in partnership with SCMAF. Both the Aquatics Coordinator
and Supervisor attended the California Water Safety Summit, California’s peak
drowning prevention conference designed to bring aquatics professionals to network,
share best practices, and work together on effective solutions to reduce drowning
statistics. These events provide great opportunities to learn valuable skills and
resources that we can bring back to South Gate.

Fitness
Our membership rate remained steady with a little over 4,100 total Fitness
memberships sold or renewed in the 3rd Quarter. Premier Memberships stayed
consistent with about 800 memberships, across the quarter. Similarly, Sports & Splash
Memberships declined slightly, which is common during the colder months when the
swimming pool is used less frequently.

Daily admissions showed an overall increase, particularly within the Sports tier. Fitness
admissions rose 15% from the previous quarter. Sports-related daily admissions
increased significantly by 26% and Volleyball usage also went up by 12%. The
increases are likely attributed to the conclusion of the Junior Athletic Association’s
basketball season, which opened more court availability for general use. Of the 4,206
total daily admissions during this quarter, 1,972 adults participated in basketball. Teens
made up the next largest group, with 533 paying for court access.

Our Personal Training program experienced a slight decrease to the number of
packages sold but maintained a consistent number of training hours delivered. This
pattern typically occurs when packages are purchased near the end of the prior quarter
and doesn’t reflect reduced demand. The Private 12-session package remained the

  Page 2 of 7
  11
 most popular option, followed by the Semi-Private 16-session package.

Lastly, the Sports Center hosted its annual Open House on Saturday, January 13, from
9 am to 1 pm. This event invited the community to experience our facility and highlight
our outstanding programming free of charge. The day included abbreviated Group
Exercise classes, program and event promotions, prize giveaways, and family-friendly
activities. A new feature this year included a vendor fair, which welcomed local
businesses such as Raising Cane’s and Celsius, marking their first-time participation in
the event. The Junior Athletic Association showcased their basketball league, with
patrons enjoying live games and participating in NBA-style halftime contests for prizes.

Youth Sports
The third quarter began with our Winter Youth Fundamentals classes, which ran from
January 6 through March 6. Attendance remained strong throughout the season, with
most classes operating near full capacity. Despite the strong start, several classes had
to be rescheduled due to the Palisade Fires and multiple rainouts during the offseason.

Following the winter session, Spring Season registration opened on March 10 and saw
record enrollment. This increase was largely due to our expanded class capacity, which
grew from 15 to 20 participants per class.

A major highlight in February was our first-ever sold-out Youth Sports field trip. On
February 13, we shuttled participants to the Galen Center on USC’s campus to watch
an exciting matchup between No. 1 UCLA and No. 4 USC Women’s Basketball teams.
The event was not only thrilling but also a meaningful experience for our young female
athletes, offering them an inspiring glimpse into the world of collegiate women’s sports.

On March 24, we hosted our annual Karate Tournament, a well-organized event that
continues to draw strong community interest. This year, we welcomed 190 athletes and
approximately 550 spectators. The tournament featured participants from Ecuador,
Nicaragua, El Salvador, and various regions across Southern California, all showcasing
their skills and passion for martial arts.

Adult Sports
The third quarter kicked off with several Fall Adult Softball divisions wrapping up their
seasons. The inaugural Women's Softball League crowned its first-ever champion,
while the Coed and Men's leagues recognized five champions across various divisions.
Winners were awarded newly designed third-quarter zip-up long sleeves, while runners-
up received custom-insulated South Gate water bottles. A total of 42 teams registered
across five divisions, including Women’s, Men’s, and Coed Softball. Spring registration
was open from March 10 to April 12, with the Spring season scheduled to begin on May
1.

Tuesday night open play volleyball remains one of our most popular drop-in activities,
with this quarter seeing a boost in attendance—totaling 650 drop-in participants.

Responding to high community demand, open play pickleball is now available Monday

  Page 3 of 7
  12
 through Friday from 1 PM to 8 PM, and Saturdays from 9 AM to 4 PM. Staff have
transformed outdoor tennis courts 1 and 2 into four dedicated pickleball courts. Daily
participation has grown, averaging 20-30 players per day.

Glow in the Dark Pickleball Night was our marquee event of the quarter. The event was
held on March 12 and had over 80 participants. They enjoyed an exciting evening
under the black lights. The Sports Center gymnasium was completely transformed into
an arena with glow-in-the-dark nets, paddles, balls, court markings, and haze machines.
All things combined with the up-tempo beats really created a vibrant and immersive
experience for everyone.

Recruitment is currently ongoing for our Men’s and Women’s Basketball Leagues.

Partner Organizations (Sports):
SG Aztecs are currently preparing for their pre-season football and cheer practices.
The Aztecs begin their pre-season training in April.

SGJAA Winter Basketball Season has concluded; teams faced off in 5 divisions and
concluded with All-Star games and practices for the top players in their respective
divisions. JAA Spring Baseball & Softball are currently conducting clinics, and the
Spring Season is set to begin on Opening Day, Saturday, May 3.

AYSO has begun practices at Hollydale Regional Park. They have increased their
number of players and teams and are preparing for their upcoming 2024 season.

Social Media:
We now have over 6,832 total followers! Last quarter we had over 20 posts, and 75
stories. We have reached over 22,975 accounts and engaged with over 1,977. We
have recently hired our new Recreation Marketing Coordinator that will oversee the
Social Media Task Force and all social media outlets. She is expected to begin at the
end of April.

Youth Programs
The Youth Programs, including Tot Time, Tiny Two’s, and Lil Chefs, had a successful
and engaging Winter session. Registration for Tot Time and Tiny Two’s began on
January 6, with most sessions reaching full capacity by January 8. Throughout the
session, children participated in fun and educational activities focused on learning
letters, shapes, and colors, while also building their motor and social skills. As the
classes progressed into their sixth week, both programs held Valentine’s Day parties
where participants exchanged cards and celebrated together. The winter session of Tot
Time and Tiny Two’s classes has concluded. In between class sessions, our Recreation
Leaders begin preparation for the next 9-week session. Staff worked on new lesson
plans, decorated classrooms, and utilized a newly created folder of arts and craft ideas
to aid in planning.

Lil Chefs began on January 21, 2025, with both Tuesday sessions fully enrolled. The
program emphasized hands-on cooking experiences, with participants making a new

  Page 4 of 7
  13
 recipe each week. Activities included creating personal pizzas, preparing heart-shaped
cakes for Valentine’s Day, and making breaded chicken tenders with yogurt parfaits in
the final class. The program successfully combined fun and education while teaching
valuable cooking skills in an interactive and engaging environment.

Special Events
The Tiaras and Ties Dance was held on January 18, 2025, at the Girls Club House.
This sold-out event celebrated the special bond between father (or special male figure)
and daughters. All attendees enjoyed a magical evening from 6:00 PM to 8:00 PM.
Guests arrived in formal attire and were treated to a lively DJ, a photo booth, and a
delicious dinner featuring chicken fettuccine alfredo, side salad, dessert, and drinks.
The evening included line dances, a traditional father-daughter dance, and the stroll.
The venue was beautifully decorated, creating an enchanting atmosphere. Each girl and
her male guest received a special gift to commemorate the night, making it a truly
unforgettable experience.

For Easter Fest 2025, our team was busy preparing for a fun-filled community event.
Eggs, bags, wristbands, and snow cone supplies have been purchased. Carnival games
and our bunny photo area supplies are also ready. DJ Gilbert, a photo booth, two face
painters, a food truck, and a soft play area have also been secured to enhance the
event overall. Our goal this year was to create lasting memories for all ages; we have
activities planned for everyone to participate in. Anyone from the age of 6 months old in
the soft play area to our seniors who can participate in our first ever adult egg hunt. The
event is sold out and set to take place next quarter.

Senior Center
This winter season was exceptionally active, with a full calendar of excursions and
events that brought our senior community together in joyful and meaningful ways.
January kicked off our winter adventures with nine scheduled trips, including visits to
Disney on Ice, Pala Casino, Palm Springs Tram, Harrah’s Casino, the Museum of Neon,
Huntington Library, Pauma Casino, the theatrical performance of Harry Potter & The
Cursed Child, and Descanso Gardens. Each of these excursions were a success, with
all trips reaching full or near-full capacity, reflecting the enthusiasm of our participants.

In February, we partnered with Alta Med to host a special Valentine’s Day event for our
seniors. With love and friendship as the theme, the event featured a DJ, a jewelry
maker, and numerous raffles, creating a festive and heartwarming atmosphere that
many seniors thoroughly enjoyed.

Continuing our commitment to supporting the emotional well-being of our seniors, our
center has maintained a strong partnership with Los Angeles Mental Health. The senior
support group, launched last year, has expanded due to high demand and now meets
three times a week, offering an essential resource for mental health support. Staying
aligned with our goal of providing monthly social gatherings, the Valentine’s Day party
marked the start of this quarter’s social events. The love in the air was tangible as
friendships flourished and long-standing couples reminded us of all the beauty of
enduring love. We distributed goodie bags, held a raffle, and honored the couple

  Page 5 of 7
  14
 married the longest with a special gift.

In March, we celebrated with a festive St. Patrick’s Day party, where the Craft Group
partnered with Alignment Health Insurance to create stunning flower arrangements.
These turned out beautifully and added a colorful touch to the celebration. Thursdays
continue to be a highlight each week, as seniors enjoy an open dance floor and lively
karaoke sessions. The energy and excitement throughout the season have been a
testament to the strength and vibrancy of our community.

Cultural Arts
The cultural arts division hosted their first Vision Board 101 workshop in January which
was a great hit! They had an attendance of 15 community members that were able to
manifest their 2025 goals. This workshop was designed to encourage teens and adults
to take time and space. Some community members asked if the division could plan just
adult programming, so we did implement that for this workshop, our Take a Break
workshop and new Adult Art Club!

After the announcement of our Playgrounds ¿Jugamos? group art exhibit we distributed
flyers, submitted flyer to quarterly city Connect, placed mini posters in city facilities and
local businesses and shared via social media. The team worked on concepts for
